author: Today I Found Out
description:
She can be found everywhere, from posters to t-shirts to coffee mugs: clad in blue coveralls, hair wrapped in a red-and-white bandana, glaring determinedly as she rolls up her sleeve, flexes her bicep, and declares: “We can do it!” Since her introduction during the Second World War, the figure of Rosie the Riveter has become a feminist icon, a potent symbol not only of the thousands of women who flooded into munitions factories and other non-traditional jobs in support of the war effort, but of limitless capabilities of all women. But how did this 80-year-old propaganda character become the iconic figure we know and love today? Was Rosie the Riveter ever an actual person, or just the product of some artist’s imagination, no more real than the scowling, finger-pointing figure of Uncle Sam? Well, as everl, the answer is complicated, but fascinating.
